design:
D1 — A reviewer verifies; it does not author. A reviewer's acceptance may carry its own reproduction: the command it ran, the output, and the commit it ran on. The accepted row then names that commit as the work it vouches for. This is not a new awaiting row, so the F500 escape stays closed: no fresh row can lift a block the operator set. The author's original summary, command and output are kept beside the reviewer's. (Operator, 2026-11-10: yes.)
D2 — The F500 guard is kept, on the requirement. Reviewer-verified acceptance is refused for a requirement whose evidence the operator has rejected on this task, and refused to the task's own author.
D3 — A missing piece goes back to the builder. Where no recorded evidence demonstrates part of a requirement, the reviewer does not fill the gap, even when it has shown that part working itself. (Operator, 2026-11-10: 'it goes back'.)
D4 — The Hub enforces the drive baseline. An acceptance-drive task's approval is refused without accepted drive_baseline evidence listing each check's outcome. The judgement that a check failed on its own assertion stays the reviewer's. (Operator, 2026-11-10: Hub-enforced.)

open_questions.question: Should a reviewer be allowed to accept evidence with its own reproduction on the task's current commit?
May a reviewer record the missing piece of a requirement it demonstrated itself, or does the task go back to the builder?
Is the drive baseline Hub-enforced, or only a rule in the reviewer's instructions?

problem:
Measured 2026-11-10 on proj-d85a82bf4216: 226 rejected evidence rows carry 140 distinct reasons across 52 tasks. Sonnet builders took 1.44 send-backs per task (151 over 105), 33 of them classed evidence-only, against 0.42 per task for Opus. Three patterns make up the paperwork share.
(1) Stale anchor. Evidence is recorded at commit A. The branch then merges master or gains a fix, the reviewer re-runs the command on the new tip and it passes, yet the reviewer still sends the task back with 'merge master and rerun', because accepted evidence decides what lands (flow tasks merge accepted evidence, not their branch tip). The reviewer may not record its own evidence (F500, requirement_evidence.py:116-136), and nothing in the Hub re-runs a command (project_checks.py:3: nothing an agent sends is ever executed).
(2) Wording or citation. The demonstration exists and the reviewer watched it pass, but the summary does not name it, or covers says partial where it is full.
(3) Unreachable or vacuous checks. Some acceptance drives stop at a 404 or 409 before their assertion, so they can never pass. Others pass against no-op code. Each is found only after the build, at review. spec_completeness.py:362-421 checks that the drive comes first in the task order, not that it fails for the right reason. Evidence kind is a free string (agent_actions.py:1798), so 'drive_baseline' and 'acceptance_drive_failing_first' are conventions, not checks.

requirements.rationale: Today an evidence row recorded before the branch moved can only be fixed by sending the task back for the author to record it again: a full builder turn that changes no code.
requirements.statement: A reviewer accepting awaiting evidence on the task it reviews may attach its own reproduction (command, output, commit). The accepted row then vouches for the reviewer's commit, and approving the task lands that commit's work, not the commit the author recorded at.

requirements.rationale: Acceptance decides what lands; a reviewer must not be able to point a task at somebody else's work.
requirements.statement: A reproduction commit must be on the task's own branch, and must be at or after the evidence's recorded commit. Otherwise the acceptance is refused with a code naming the commit.

requirements.rationale: The operator reading the evidence must be able to tell what the builder claimed from what the reviewer saw.
requirements.statement: When a reviewer accepts with a reproduction or corrects summary or covers, the evidence keeps the author's original summary, command, output and covers, and shows the reviewer's beside them, attributed to the reviewer and its run.

requirements.rationale: F500: a reviewer's own fresh evidence once lifted the operator's rejection and let the reviewer approve over it.
requirements.statement: Reviewer-verified acceptance is refused for a requirement where the operator has rejected evidence on this task, and is refused to the agent that authored the evidence. A reviewer still cannot record a new awaiting evidence row on the task it reviews.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-10: a gap in what was demonstrated goes back to the builder.
requirements.statement: Where no recorded evidence demonstrates part of a requirement, the reviewer cannot accept that evidence as covering the whole requirement, and cannot record the missing piece. It sends the task back naming the missing piece.

A task that is a document's acceptance drive cannot be approved without accepted evidence of kind drive_baseline. That evidence lists, for each acceptance check the drive covers, whether the check was reached on the pre-build code and whether it failed at its own assertion. The refusal names the missing baseline.

requirements.rationale: Of the rejected evidence on record, about a quarter were checks that could never pass, or passed against no-op code, and were found only after the whole build.
requirements.statement: A drive baseline in which any covered check was not reached (it stopped at setup, a 404 or 409, or a crash), or passed on the pre-build code, is not accepted. The reviewer sends the drive task back naming each such check.

The model record and the build retrospective report evidence-only send-backs per task, and reviewer-verified acceptances per task, so the change's effect is visible against the 2026-11-10 baseline (Sonnet 33 evidence-only send-backs over 105 tasks).

in_scope: A reviewer accepting evidence with its own reproduction on the task's current commit, and that commit becoming what the evidence vouches for
A reviewer correcting an accepted row's summary and covers, kept beside the author's
A Hub-enforced per-check baseline for the acceptance-drive task, and its review
Reporting evidence-only send-backs and reviewer-verified acceptances per task, so the effect can be measured
non_goals: The Hub executing any agent-supplied command: project checks remain the only thing the Hub runs
A reviewer recording the missing piece of a requirement: a gap goes back to the builder
Removing evidence review, or approving work without accepted evidence
Changing what the operator may do with evidence (accept, reject, reopen)
Fixing the model record counting a task under its reviewer's model (a pre-existing defect found while measuring; it goes to the backlog, not into this change)
Mechanically proving that a check failed for the right reason: that stays the reviewer's judgement

summary: Evidence review is the stage that catches work that passes its own tests but cannot fire. About half of the 140 distinct rejection reasons on record are real defects, and a quarter are checks that could never pass or passed without testing anything. The last fifth or so are paperwork: evidence recorded at a commit that has since moved, or a summary that cites too little. Each of those costs a full builder turn and a full review turn. After this change, a reviewer who can reproduce the demonstration accepts it as it stands on the current work. An acceptance drive cannot be approved until it is shown reaching each check and failing there, so 'this check can never pass' is caught before the build, not after it.
